title: Add snapshot-based state preservation and downgrade guardrails for private installer
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: production private upgrades exposed a class of failures where partial schema migrations combined with controller restarts left clusters in a nonrecoverable state. This PR introduces a snapshot-first upgrade flow and an explicit downgrade guard that prevents accidental rollbacks unless a verified restore snapshot exists. High level changes: 1) rpictl snapshot create/restore commands (CLI + install hooks) that create a consistent data snapshot (Postgres logical dump + object storage of blobstore pointers) prior to any upgrade; 2) Helm hooks to trigger pre-upgrade snapshot job and a post-upgrade health-check job that auto-rolls back on detectable data drift; 3) a migration-runner job that validates schema diffs in dry-run mode and fails the upgrade if forward-only migrations would be irreversible; 4) Terraform module updates to provision a dedicated snapshot bucket (S3-compatible) with lifecycle + encryption, plus state-lock improvements to avoid concurrent upgrades; 5) an explicit downgrade-blocker controller that checks release semver and snapshot provenance and rejects a lower-version apply unless --force-downgrade is passed with validated snapshot id. Backwards compatibility: installer still works without snapshot bucket (legacy mode) but the new guardrails are enabled by default for new deployments. Checklist: - [x] rpictl CLI + docs - [x] Helm charts and hooks - [x] migration-runner image and manifests - [x] Terraform module + tests - [x] e2e upgrade test using KIND + local S3 emulator - [x] security review (KMS + bucket policy) Rollout plan: feature flag gated for existing clusters; default-on for new installs. Related: Linear ENG-9821 (upgrade resilience), ENG-9902 (terraform snapshot infra). Links: internal runbook https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-9821/upgrade-resilience, design doc https://redwood.internal/docs/installer-snapshots.

review_comments: Miguel Ortega: Please ensure snapshot uploads use multipart for >5GB clusters; also add metrics for snapshot duration.

testing: Unit: CLI + controller unit tests run locally (go test) and on CI
Integration: e2e upgrade test using KIND + minio passed in CI (integration-e2e), validates snapshot creation and restore flow
Load: simulated snapshot on 200GB logical workload tested in staging, average upload 12m with multipart enabled
Security: KMS envelope encryption validated, bucket policy restricts access to installer service account
rollback_plan: If a release fails post-upgrade health checks the post-upgrade hook triggers a Helm rollback automatically; manual rollback steps: 1) rpictl snapshot restore --id <snapshot-id> --wait to restore DB and blob pointers, 2) helm rollback <release> <revision> via the console, 3) monitor health-checks and open INCIDENT if state mismatch persists. For emergency downgrades, use --force-downgrade with a verified snapshot id and coordinate with on-call; audit-log entries are required.
security_implications: Snapshot uploads require S3-compatible storage with server-side encryption and KMS key access limited to installer/service-account. The admission webhook enforces provenance checks; no plaintext credentials are added to manifests. Terraform changes ensure ACME of bucket policies; security-scan in CI passes. See docs for KMS key rotation guidance.
release_notes: Added snapshot-first upgrade flow and automatic downgrade guardrails for private installer: rpictl snapshot commands, Helm pre/post upgrade hooks, migration-runner dry-run validation, Terraform snapshot bucket module, and an admission webhook to block accidental downgrades. These changes are opt-in for existing clusters and enabled by default for new installs.
